## §54. Owner-Approved = LOCKED / Regression-Protected — PERMANENT REQUIREMENT (added 2026-08-30, Owner-Locked Regression Rule task, Owner-established)

**Owner decision, standing rule, applies to ALL future ProFlow work — not scoped to any single item, does not expire, does not need to be re-requested.**

**The rule**: once a behavior, design, feature, or fix has (1) been implemented, (2) been TEST-verified, and (3) been reviewed/accepted by the Owner, it becomes **Owner-Approved / DONE / LOCKED / regression-protected**. From that point forward it must not change unless the Owner explicitly authorizes reopening or changing it. Covers, without exception: behavior, functionality, layout, visual styling, copy/text, responsive behavior, HE behavior, EN behavior, Local behavior, International behavior, calculations, business rules, permissions, workflows, and every previously-approved fix.

**No indirect changes.** A new task is never itself authorization to alter unrelated LOCKED behavior — including indirectly, through refactoring, shared CSS, responsive CSS, component cleanup, dependency changes, layout changes, design-system changes, code deduplication, performance optimization, translation work, HE/EN parity work, mobile fixes, desktop fixes, accessibility work, feature implementation elsewhere, or bug fixes elsewhere. "Improvement," "cleaner code," and "better design" are explicitly **not** authorization to touch LOCKED behavior.

**Regression protection is engineering's responsibility, not the Owner's.** The Owner must not have to repeatedly remember or manually re-verify whether something previously completed still works — that burden belongs to Claude Lead, Agent HE, Agent EN, and the test process. Once Owner-approved and LOCKED, the Owner is entitled to treat it as finished. If a later task causes a LOCKED item to change unexpectedly, that is a **regression**, to be caught and reported as such, not normalized away.

**Required stop condition**: if a genuinely new feature/fix requires changing an existing LOCKED behavior, **STOP before changing it** and report: what LOCKED behavior would need to change, why, alternatives considered, HE impact, EN impact, Local impact, International impact, and regression risk — then wait for explicit Owner authorization. Approval is never inferred from the new task's own existence or scope.

**Enforcement mechanism — uses existing structures, does not duplicate them with a new ledger.** Per explicit Owner instruction not to create unnecessary documentation duplication, this rule does **not** introduce a new tracking document. LOCKED state is the mechanisms already in continuous use across the six canonical files, now formally designated as this rule's enforcement surface:
- A `PROFLOW_TODO.md` item marked `🟢 COMPLETE / VERIFIED` (or `TEST VERIFIED`, `Owner visually accepted`, etc.) **is**, from that point, Owner-Approved/LOCKED under this rule — §47's existing "never delete a completed TODO item" discipline already protects its historical record; this rule adds that its *content/behavior* must also not silently drift.
- A `PROFLOW_HANDOFF.md` §18 step recording a verdict of `PASS` (Owner-reviewed or explicitly accepted) is a LOCKED checkpoint for whatever it describes.
- The existing **File-by-File HE/EN Change Ledger** (§37, cross-market tasks) is the concrete mechanism for identifying exactly which files/surfaces a given LOCKED item touches — a future task working near a LOCKED file should consult the ledger entry that last touched it before assuming a change is safe.
- Before any task changes a file/surface that a prior `PASS`/`COMPLETE`/`VERIFIED` entry already covers, that entry is the signal to check first — if the planned change would alter what was previously verified, this is the **stop condition** above, not a green light.

**Relationship to existing rules**: this rule does not replace §36 (Test-First/Owner-Gated Live Release), §37 (HE/EN Parity), or §38 (Effort-Level Declaration) — it adds a durable "once accepted, stays accepted" guarantee on top of them. §36 already requires Owner approval before LIVE; this rule extends that same approval's weight forward in time, protecting the approved result from later, unrelated erosion.

**Addendum (added 2026-08-31, Owner-established, carried forward explicitly from the Critical Signature Security Production Promotion task so it is not lost after that promotion)**: OWNER-APPROVED/LOCKED protects **observable behavior**, not merely a specific file or component. A change to a shared/parent/layout component, or a refactor, that never touches the LOCKED component's own file but changes what a user actually sees/experiences at that LOCKED surface is still a regression under this rule — "I didn't edit that file" is not a defense. Any task touching a shared/parent/layout surface must regression-test every LOCKED behavior that surface affects, even when the LOCKED component itself was not directly edited. One concrete, already-documented instance of this principle: §61's **"responsive transformations must preserve functional capability, not merely visible content"** rule (a Desktop capability — e.g., column sorting — silently absent after a Mobile responsive transformation is a regression, even though no single component was "deleted").

Desktop — use available screen width** (`src/index.css`, `src/pages/Dashboard.jsx`): audited the existing shared `--pf-desktop-content-width` (980px) token first and found it is used by **both** the authenticated app shell (`Dashboard.jsx`, all tabs) **and** Public Quote (`PublicQuote.jsx`/`PublicQuoteEn.jsx`) — the latter's 980px value is itself an extensively-verified, Owner-locked value from an earlier dedicated Global Surface Audit (shell-padding/border `calc()` math specifically reverse-engineered to make the *visible content* exactly 980px). Public Quote was **not** named in this task's own regression-check list. Per §54 (no indirect changes to LOCKED behavior established in this very same task), widening the shared token would have silently also widened the separately-locked, unaudited-this-task Public Quote surface. **Decoupled instead**: a new, dedicated CSS variable `--pf-dashboard-desktop-content-width: 1440px` now governs only the authenticated app's content wrapper (`Dashboard.jsx` line ~2910); `--pf-desktop-content-width` remains exactly `980px`, untouched, still used only by Public Quote. Live-verified: Dashboard content wrapper now measures ~1405px (up from 980px) at a 1440px viewport, identical in both markets; Public Quote's own token confirmed still reading `980px` via a live `getComputedStyle` check on `document.documentElement` — genuinely unaffected. Regression-verified at Dashboard/New Quote/Quote History/Clients/Business Settings (all render inside the same single wrapper, so one check covers all) — zero horizontal overflow at any tested width, Client Type badge and other existing UI unaffected. Admin layout not touched (out of scope, untouched by construction — Admin does not use this wrapper).

**4. Trial notice vertical position** (`src/pages/Dashboard.jsx`): root cause — both notice variants (`dash-trial-slidebar` for expiring/expired, `dash-trial-ticker-lane` for a plain active trial) are `position: absolute; top: 100%` children of `.dash-header-bar`, occupying the gap between the purple header and the nav row below — but the header's own `marginBottom` (14px, unconditional) was shorter than either notice's actual footprint (~44-52px for the card variant, ~36px for the ticker), so the notice's own bottom edge extended into where the nav row begins, matching the Owner's observed collision. **Fixed by giving the notice a dedicated safe vertical lane, not by redesigning it**: a new derived `hasVisibleTrialNotice` boolean conditionally raises `.dash-header-bar`'s `marginBottom` from `14px` to `64px` **only while a notice is actually visible** — zero change to the header/nav gap the rest of the time (the default, most-common state), and zero change to either notice's own text, color, motion, timing, or "no card/background" design (both LOCKED, per the Owner's explicit instruction not to redesign them). Live-verified, both markets: notice bottom edge measured at 104px, nav row top edge at 132px — 28px of clear separation, `collision: false`, confirmed via direct bounding-box measurement, not just visual inspection; also confirmed visually via full-page screenshots.

**Verification summary**: all four fixes live-verified together, both markets (HE/Local via `PROFLOW_TEST_LOCAL_*`, EN/International via `PROFLOW_TEST_INTL_*`), desktop (1440px) and mobile (360/390/412px) — zero horizontal overflow anywhere, zero regression in the Client Type badge (§26), the Trial Expiration → FREE fix (§51), or any other previously-approved UI. 70/70 automated tests pass (Trial Expiration tests preserved and re-confirmed green), lint clean, build succeeds.

## §56. ProFlow Global Surface Width Contract — PERMANENT REQUIREMENT (added 2026-08-30, Owner Visual QA Correction task, Owner-established)

**Owner decision, standing rule, applies to ALL future ProFlow work — not scoped to any single screen, does not expire.**

**The rule**: ProFlow must have ONE canonical responsive content-width strategy. The same canonical strategy must govern equivalent full-page product surfaces across the product — authenticated application (Dashboard, Quote History, New Quote, Clients, Business Settings, Catalog, Finances), HE, EN, Local, International, and Public Quote/displayed-quote presentation, unless the Owner explicitly approves a documented exception. At the same viewport width, HE and EN must have the same overall content geometry; Local and International must have the same overall content geometry.

**RTL/LTR is not a functional-reason exception.** Language is not a functional-reason exception. Market is not a functional-reason exception. Direction may change element order/alignment/mirroring — it must never change the canonical overall content width. A width difference is permitted only when there is a genuine functional reason **and** the Owner explicitly approves that specific, documented exception.

**One source of truth, not accumulated arbitrary widths.** The desired architecture is one canonical width contract/token that equivalent surfaces reference, rather than each screen independently choosing its own max-width, padding, or container strategy. Where consolidating an existing surface onto the canonical contract would modify Owner-LOCKED geometry (§54), the LOCKED rule's stop condition applies: audit and report the conflict, do not silently change it, wait for explicit Owner authorization for that specific surface.

**Relationship to §54**: this rule defines *what* the canonical contract should eventually cover; §54 governs *when* a specific numeric implementation of it becomes protected. A width value is never Owner-Approved/LOCKED merely because it satisfies this contract's architecture — it still requires the Owner's own explicit visual approval of that specific result (see §57).

HE/EN parity was never broken and remains fully preserved.

The Owner's new visual reference suggested content occupying roughly 70-75% of the viewport, explicitly described as an unconfirmed initial reference, not a hard-coded percentage.

Live-confirmed **no clipping** at any tested width, both markets (`actionsFullyVisible: true`, and the table's own measured box now exactly matches its wrapper's box at every width — the earlier clipping run showed the table box overflowing past its wrapper, a reliable signal of the same defect). **Mobile Quote History width utilization — root cause and fix**: the "Recent Quotes History" panel wrapper (`QuotesTab.jsx`) used a single, uniform `padding: '14px'` on both desktop and mobile — combined with `.dash-main-content`'s mobile override (`6px`, pre-existing) and each mobile card's own internal padding (`8px 10px`, pre-existing, unchanged), this produced a genuinely compounded ~30px gutter on each side before any card content began — the exact anti-pattern the Owner described. Fixed narrowly: the panel's own `isMobileView` state (already used by this exact component to switch between the desktop table and mobile card list) now also drives its padding — `8px` on mobile, unchanged `14px` on desktop. Live-verified, both markets, 360/390/412px: total page gutter now `15px` each side (down from ~30px), card width `330px` at 360px viewport (91.7% utilization), zero horizontal overflow at any width, byte-identical between HE and EN at every measurement.

**Amount typography hierarchy (round 2)**: Rubik is self-hosted with explicit weight files for 400/500/600/700/800/900 (both Latin and Hebrew subsets, `src/fonts.css`) — `500` is a genuine, distinctly-rendering weight, not a synthetic fallback, confirmed before changing anything. Quote History row amount (`QuotesTab.jsx`, desktop table and mobile card): `600 → 500`. Dashboard Total Revenue/`סך הכנסות` (`Dashboard.jsx`, the `.dash-kpi-value.pf-money` element specifically — confirmed via direct DOM ancestor-chain inspection, not a generic class query, since more than one `.dash-kpi-value` element exists on the page and a naive selector can match the wrong one): `800 → 600`. ## Incident Record — Continuity Sync Execution Failure, Corrected 2026-08-30 (Continuity Sync Failure Audit + Recovery task — NOT a new permanent rule, disclosed per this project's standing incident-transparency practice)

**What happened**: across three consecutive tasks this session (bootstrap, TEST Acceptance Readiness Package 1, Client Type Badge), the six canonical files were correctly updated in the main working tree, and every task's Final Report accurately stated so — but the separate, already-established continuity-sync step (§17.J's "Claude local → isolated continuity worktree → secret/privacy scan → explicit staging → commit on `proflow-continuity` → push **only** `proflow-continuity`") was never executed. ChatGPT subsequently read `ref=proflow-continuity` on GitHub directly and found it stale (last commit `998f1bd`, predating this entire session) — `PROFLOW_CLAUDE_LATEST_REPORT.md` there did not contain the Client Type Badge report, and `PROFLOW_TODO.md` there lacked items 27/28.

**Root cause**: task-level instructions this session repeatedly stated "NO commit. NO push." — correctly scoped to **application code on `main`** (per every task's own surrounding context: paired with "NO Vercel deploy," "NO Production/LIVE action," etc.). §17.J already establishes that continuity-branch documentation sync is a **separate, standing, routinely-authorized layer** ("DOCUMENTATION SYNC AUTHORIZATION ≠ ... ≠ CONTINUITY PUSH AUTHORIZATION ≠ MAIN PUSH AUTHORIZATION"), verified safe (no Vercel deployment consequence) specifically so it would **not** need to wait for the same authorization as `main`. The execution failure was conflating the two: treating "no commit/push" as blanket guidance covering documentation too, when the existing architecture already treats them as entirely distinct.

**Correction applied same task**: the isolated continuity worktree (`quotecode-saas-continuity`, checked out on `proflow-continuity`) was updated with the current six files, diffed and secret/privacy-scanned (clean), staged explicitly by name (never `git add -A`), committed (`d4a6b03`), and pushed to `proflow-continuity` only. **Read back directly from GitHub** (via the GitHub REST Contents API against `ref=proflow-continuity`, not local git cache) to confirm all six files are present and current, `PROFLOW_CLAUDE_LATEST_REPORT.md` contains the Client Type Badge report, and `PROFLOW_TODO.md` contains items 27/28 — all confirmed. `main`'s HEAD (local and remote) was unchanged throughout (`17ac4d3a...`); no application file was staged, committed, or touched.

**No new permanent rule was added.** §17.J already fully covers this; the fix is executional (actually perform the existing step at the end of each task), not architectural. Future sessions: perform the §17.J continuity-branch sync at the end of every meaningful task, independent of whatever application-code commit/push authorization state is in force for that same task — the two are unrelated gates.

## §58. Customer-Signature Authorization — Forensic Findings + Permanent Customer-Only-Actions Rule (added 2026-08-30, Critical Signature Forensic Audit task)

**Permanent intended product rule (documented separately from the fresh technical findings below, per this task's own explicit instruction not to conflate the two)**: CUSTOMER-ONLY ACTIONS MUST REMAIN CUSTOMER-ONLY. A business-side user must never gain customer-side approval/signature authority as a side effect of refactoring, shared components, route reuse, auth changes, HE/EN work, responsive work, UI changes, or feature development. Changing this boundary requires explicit Owner authorization. UI hiding alone is never sufficient to satisfy this rule — the authoritative enforcement must exist at the mutation/persistence boundary.

**Fresh forensic findings (this task, evidence-based, not guessed)**:

- **Signing path traced end to end**: `PublicQuote.jsx`/`PublicQuoteEn.jsx` (`handleApprove`) -> `useSignaturePad.js` (canvas capture, shared hook, identical both markets) -> `supabase.rpc('public_approve_quote', { p_quote_id, p_signature_data_url })` -> Postgres function `public.public_approve_quote(uuid,text)` (`SECURITY DEFINER`, owner `postgres`, `search_path` pinned, `EXECUTE` granted to `anon`+`authenticated`, `PUBLIC` revoked -- captured faithfully from live Production in `supabase/migrations/20260830000001_capture_base_functions_triggers.sql`).
- **The RPC's actual body validates only**: quote id present, signature is a non-empty, size-capped, regex-valid `data:image/png;base64,...` string, and the target row's current `status` is `draft`/`sent` with an empty `signature` (one atomic conditional `UPDATE`). **It contains no reference to `auth.uid()` anywhere, no ownership check, no anonymous-only requirement, no customer-specific token.** `guard_quote_immutability()` (the other quotes-table guard trigger) only fires once a quote is ALREADY approved/paid/signed -- it provides zero protection against the FIRST transition into that state, contrary to what the original Aug 25 remediation's own documentation implied ("existing quote immutability trigger remains an independent lower-layer guard").
- **UI-layer protection that DOES exist and DOES work correctly**: `get-public-quote` (Edge Function, service_role) computes `is_owner_viewing: Boolean(callerUserId && callerUserId === quote.user_id)` from the caller's own Authorization header (present automatically via `supabase.functions.invoke` whenever the browser tab holds an authenticated session) -- when true, `PublicQuote.jsx`/`PublicQuoteEn.jsx` hide the signing canvas/button entirely and show an "admin view, signature area is customer-only" notice instead. This correctly protects the specific case of a quote's own creator opening their own link in the same authenticated browser tab. **It provides no protection whatsoever against (a) a direct call to the RPC bypassing the UI, by anyone -- the quote's own owner, a different authenticated business account, or an anonymous script with the quote id -- or (b) any authenticated business user (not just the quote's own owner) opening a DIFFERENT business's quote link, since for them `is_owner_viewing` is false and they see the normal, fully-functional customer signing UI, identical to a genuine customer.**
- **Live TEST reproduction (Owner-authorized, TEST/local mutation only, no Production interaction)**: signed in as `PROFLOW_TEST_LOCAL_EMAIL` via ordinary `signInWithPassword` (the established, precedented credential-use pattern, §22), selected one of that account's own `draft` quotes with no existing signature, and called `public_approve_quote` directly via the TEST project's REST RPC endpoint using that session's own access token -- bypassing `PublicQuote.jsx` entirely. Result: **HTTP 204**. Re-queried the same quote immediately after: `status` = `approved`, `signature` = a 114-character valid PNG data URL, both persisted. This is a direct, reproduced demonstration of a business user persisting customer-role approval/signature state on their own quote, exactly the Owner-suspected scenario.
- **Historical integrity -- what can and cannot be proven**: the `quotes` table has no column recording who or what performed an approval (no `signed_by`, no approver role, no IP/session marker) -- only `status` and a raw `signature` base64 blob. **What CAN be proven**: the mutation path has no server-side identity check today, and is TEST-confirmed exploitable by an authenticated business session. **What CANNOT be proven**: whether any specific existing/historical signature on any real quote (TEST or Production) was actually created this way rather than by a genuine customer -- there is no data trail to distinguish the two. No historical signature has been or should be treated as invalid based on this finding alone; none were altered.
- **Previous protection -- proven vs. unknown**: the original "Public Quote Security Remediation" commit (`1caaff6`, 2026-08-25) that created `public_approve_quote` documented, for the sibling `public_increment_quote_view` RPC, "live tests passed for anon, owner, different authenticated TEST user" -- but recorded **no equivalent owner/different-user test for `public_approve_quote` itself**, only functional payload-validation tests. There is no evidence in git history that the RPC's identity check was ever present and later removed. **Conclusion: UNKNOWN whether this is a true regression of something that once worked; the more evidence-supported characterization is an unclosed gap present since the RPC's original creation, not a subsequently-removed protection.** The `is_owner_viewing` UI guard itself has not regressed and is unchanged/working.
- **HE impact**: AFFECTED -- `PublicQuote.jsx` calls the identical RPC with identical parameters. **EN impact**: AFFECTED -- `PublicQuoteEn.jsx` calls the identical RPC with identical parameters. Both markets share one signing path; there is no market-specific protection to compare.
- **Production exposure -- read-only evidence only, no live Production query or mutation performed**: `supabase/migrations/20260830000001_capture_base_functions_triggers.sql`'s own header states every function in that file, `public_approve_quote` included, was "captured EXACTLY as it is defined live on Production today" (captured 2026-08-30, i.e., very recently). That captured body is the same zero-identity-check definition found and TEST-reproduced above. **PRODUCTION POTENTIALLY AFFECTED: YES**, on this documentary evidence -- no Production quote was signed/approved/mutated/queried to reach this conclusion.
- **Recommended minimal safe fix (proposal only -- NOT implemented this task)**: add an authorization check inside `public_approve_quote` that rejects the call whenever the caller is identifiable as ANY ProFlow business account (`auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM business_settings WHERE user_id = auth.uid())`) -- not merely "caller equals this quote's own owner," since that narrower check would still leave the cross-account gap open. Anonymous/genuine-customer approval (the intended, legitimate path) is unaffected by this check.
- **Required regression tests for any future fix (proposal only)**: (1) anonymous/customer approval still succeeds; (2) the quote's own authenticated business owner calling the RPC directly is rejected; (3) a different authenticated business account calling the RPC on someone else's quote is rejected; (4) `is_owner_viewing` UI hide still functions unchanged; (5) `guard_quote_immutability` still blocks post-approval edits; (6) both HE and EN re-verified, since they share the RPC; (7) the frontend's existing generic error-toast handling still degrades gracefully for a legitimately-rejected direct-API call.

**No remediation was implemented this task -- audit only, per explicit instruction.** No Production quote was signed, approved, mutated, or used for testing; no existing signature was modified; all reproduction used TEST-only data. The mutated TEST quote's approved/signed state was NOT reverted, since the immutability trigger blocks reverting an approved/signed quote by design -- this is disclosed, not hidden.

## §60. Critical Signature Authorization Fix — PRODUCTION DEPLOYED / VERIFIED (added 2026-08-31, Signature Fix + Mobile Cleanup + Email Audit + Lock Final Width task; promoted to Production same day, Critical Signature Security Production Promotion task)

Following §58's forensic audit, the Owner authorized audit-reconfirmation, implementation, and TEST verification of a fix (still no Production action of any kind).

**Audit reconfirmation before touching anything**: `supabase db dump --linked` against `quotecode-test` confirmed the live `public_approve_quote` definition was byte-identical to the one captured in `20260830000001_capture_base_functions_triggers.sql` and to what §58 analyzed — no drift, safe to proceed from that exact known state.

**Business-account identification — reused, not invented**: `business_settings.user_id` (one row per business/user) is the exact same source of truth `is_admin()`/`is_super_admin()` already use for "is this uid a ProFlow account" checks. No new identity table was created.

**Fix design — deliberately broader than "equals this quote's owner"**: the RPC now rejects the call whenever `auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM business_settings WHERE user_id = auth.uid())` — i.e., any authenticated ProFlow business account at all, not merely the specific quote's own creator. A narrower `auth.uid() = quotes.user_id` check would still leave a different authenticated business account free to sign someone else's quote, indistinguishable from a genuine customer to that narrower check. Anonymous callers (`auth.uid() IS NULL`, the legitimate Public Quote flow) are completely unaffected — every other existing validation (payload shape/size, status/signature-empty precondition) is byte-identical to the previously-captured definition.

**Applied to TEST only**: new migration `supabase/migrations/20260831000000_fix_public_approve_quote_business_check.sql`, applied via `supabase db push` while the CLI was linked to `quotecode-test` (`ljfizgrdyzxddswcedwr`) — the CLI was relinked back to Production (`ixabnzhjeqevtbhdfswv`, `linked:true`) immediately afterward, per the standing session convention (§18.N). Production was never linked-to or mutated.

## §62. P1 Full Reconciliation + Session Timeout Forensic Audit — AUDIT ONLY, NO IMPLEMENTATION (added 2026-08-31, P1 Full Reconciliation task)

**Scope note**: no document in this project's canonical continuity set uses a literal "P1" label on any backlog item. This audit treats "P1" as the open/audit-required items in the Master Product TODO (`PROFLOW_TODO.md` items 1-11, 15, 19-21, 22-25) that are not already fully COMPLETE/VERIFIED and are not among this task's own explicitly excluded categories (Admin, Item 28/30/31, Landing Page, Vercel/domain, new-feature work). The full item-by-item ledger is in this task's chat report (not duplicated here in full) — this section records only what is new/verified this task.

### Session Timeout — Forensic Findings

**No ProFlow application-level session-timeout mechanism exists anywhere in this codebase.** This is a strong, evidence-based negative finding, not an assumption:

- `src/shared/supabase.js` (the sole Supabase client instantiation) passes zero custom `auth` options — no `autoRefreshToken`, `persistSession`, `detectSessionInUrl`, or session-lifetime override of any kind. It uses supabase-js v2's pure platform defaults (`autoRefreshToken: true`, `persistSession: true`) — normal JWT background refresh, not a ProFlow-authored timeout.
- A repo-wide search for `lastActivity`, `idleTimer`, `inactivity`, `session-timeout`/`sessionTimeout` found matches only inside the six continuity documents (all references to the still-open TODO item 8 itself) — zero matches in `src/`.
- `package.json` has no idle/inactivity-detection dependency of any kind.
- `supabase.auth.signOut()` is called from exactly one place in the entire codebase: `Dashboard.jsx`'s `handleSignOut`, itself only reachable via the explicit user-clicked Sign Out button → `SignOutModal` confirm callback. No timer, no automatic path, no other caller exists anywhere.
- Every `onAuthStateChange` listener in the app (`App.jsx`, `AppLocal.jsx`, `AppGlobal.jsx`, `Dashboard.jsx`) reacts normally to `SIGNED_IN`/`SIGNED_OUT`/`TOKEN_REFRESHED`/`PASSWORD_RECOVERY` events by updating local React state — none contain custom timeout/expiry logic, none force a logout independent of an actual Supabase-emitted `SIGNED_OUT` event.
- Every `setTimeout`/`setInterval` found in `src/` was individually traced and is unrelated to auth: a hot-quote-carousel rotation (4s), an exchange-rate refetch (10min, two public calculator widgets), a generic 10-minute UI-refresh tick (`setLiveTick`, drives "recently active" client-list indicators and time-relative displays — confirmed it never touches `session` state or calls `signOut`), and date-math for the 14-day trial period (unrelated to session lifetime).

**Root cause of the Owner-observed timeout behavior: UNKNOWN, but NOT a ProFlow application timeout (ruled out with high confidence).** Two remaining, unruled-out candidates, both outside this repository's own code and therefore not confirmable or deniable from a source-code audit alone:
1. **Normal Supabase refresh-token lifecycle** (a genuine "Type B" per this task's own taxonomy) — if a background token refresh ever fails (network blip, a long-suspended/backgrounded browser tab throttling the scheduled refresh timer, a corrupted/cleared `localStorage` entry), supabase-js emits a real `SIGNED_OUT` event and the user is shown the login screen — indistinguishable, from the Owner's perspective, from "the app logged me out."
2. **A Supabase-project-level Auth session policy** (a genuine "Type D") — Supabase's Auth product supports project-level session settings (e.g., an absolute session lifetime / inactivity timeout) configurable only via the Supabase Dashboard's Auth settings, entirely outside this Git repository. This cannot be confirmed or denied by auditing application source code. **Not checked this task** — the Supabase CLI has no read command for this setting, and attempting a raw Management API call (which was not clearly established as safe/precedented in this project's history, and could return other sensitive Auth-provider configuration alongside it) was deliberately not attempted without further explicit authorization. **Recommended next step**: the Owner directly inspects Supabase Dashboard → Authentication → Sessions/Settings for both the Production and `quotecode-test` projects, or explicitly authorizes a separate, scoped, read-only Management API task to do so.

**LOCAL/TEST/PRODUCTION/HE/EN**: no application-controlled timeout exists in the source code that ships to any of these environments — the code is identical everywhere. Whether the unconfirmed platform-level setting (candidate 2 above) differs between the Production and TEST Supabase projects is itself unknown and was not checked.

**Multi-device impact**: not applicable today — there is no ProFlow-authored session policy of any kind to conflict with simultaneous multi-device logins. Supabase's default `persistSession`+`autoRefreshToken` behavior (unmodified) inherently supports independent simultaneous sessions per device, each with its own local refresh cycle.

**No code was modified to investigate this. No session was deliberately destroyed on TEST or Production to test this.**

### Behavioral Lock Rules — Verified Present and Coherent

Confirmed via direct read of canonical continuity (not merely trusting the latest Claude report): §54's addendum ("OWNER-APPROVED/LOCKED protects observable behavior, not merely a specific file or component... shared/parent/layout/refactor changes must regression-test affected LOCKED behavior even when the LOCKED component itself was not directly edited") and §61's responsive-capability rule ("responsive transformations must preserve functional capability, not merely visible content") are both present, intact, and internally consistent — the former is the general principle, the latter its first concrete documented instance.

Nothing in this inventory is newly implemented by this task; it is a read-only snapshot of pre-existing state.

## §63. PERMANENT RULE — HE/EN Directional Symmetry (Inline-Start Contract) (added 2026-08-31, Mobile-Only HE/EN Directional Mirroring Fix task, Owner-established)

**The rule**: whenever a ProFlow UI structure has a defined semantic order in Hebrew/RTL, the corresponding English/LTR structure must preserve the **same semantic order**, measured from each language's own **inline-start edge** (right in RTL, left in LTR). RTL/LTR changes physical direction; it must never change semantic priority/order.

```
HE / RTL:  RIGHT (inline-start) → A → B → C
EN / LTR:  LEFT  (inline-start) → A → B → C
```

**NOT** a reversed sequence between languages (`HE: A→B→C` vs `EN: C→B→A`) — that is a **violation** of this rule, not a valid mirror, unless the Owner explicitly approves a different semantic order for a specific surface.

**The contract is measured as "1st/2nd/3rd from inline-start,"** never as hard-coded "left"/"right" — this is what prevents the exact misinterpretation this task corrected. For the Mobile Quote History card specifically, the permanent contract is:

- **Position 1 from inline-start**: Client Type
- **Position 2 from inline-start**: Views
- **Position 3 from inline-start**: Client Name
- (Amount remains at the opposite/outer edge, per the existing separately-approved layout — unaffected by this rule)

HE inline-start = right. EN inline-start = left. **Desktop Quote History is explicitly NOT part of this specific Mobile ordering contract** and remains separately LOCKED/unmodified by this rule.

**Implementation guidance**: the correct, robust way to satisfy this contract is a single, language-**non-conditional** DOM/element order, combined with the existing `dir="rtl"`/`dir="ltr"` attribute already present on the containing element — the browser's own RTL/LTR layout engine (flex or grid) then places the first element at each language's inline-start automatically. A language-**conditional** DOM order (`isHebrew ? [A,B,C] : [C,B,A]`) is very likely a symptom of this exact violation, not a correct mirror — it produces a literal sequence-reversal instead of true directional mirroring. This matches the pattern already used successfully elsewhere in `QuotesTab.jsx`'s own mobile card (the order#/date/status row) and is now also how the Client Type/Views/Client Name/Amount row is implemented.

**Relationship to existing rules**: this is a concrete, permanent instance of §54's "OWNER-APPROVED/LOCKED protects observable behavior" principle — the semantic order itself, not just its current implementation, is now the protected behavior. It is a sibling rule to §61's "responsive transformations must preserve functional capability" — both protect what a user actually experiences at a LOCKED surface, one across viewport-size transformations, this one across language/direction transformations.

**Root cause of why this was not caught earlier (Owner's explicit question)**: this was **not** a case of independent HE-agent-PASS / EN-agent-PASS masking a real defect through insufficient cross-checking, though that risk is real and addressed below. The direct root cause is that an **earlier explicit Owner instruction, in a prior task this session, literally specified the reversed-sequence version** ("HE: Client Type → Views → Client Name" / "EN, mirror this logically: Client Name → Views → Client Type") — that instruction was followed exactly, implemented, and TEST-verified as specified. Both HE and EN individually matched their own specification perfectly; the specification itself embedded the now-corrected misconception (treating "mirror" as "reverse the sequence" rather than "preserve the sequence from each side's own start"). No agent or verification step failed to catch a deviation from spec — the spec itself needed the Owner's own correction, which this task now implements. This is disclosed plainly, not attributed to a process failure that didn't occur.

**Permanent process strengthening (the risk that IS real and now addressed)**: even when a specification is correct, independent HE-PASS + EN-PASS verification is **not sufficient** to catch a directional-symmetry defect, because each side can correctly match its own half of an incorrect (or ambiguous) spec while the pair fails true mirroring. **New standing verification requirement**: for any shared HE/EN UI contract with a defined element order, verification must report each element's **position counted from inline-start** (not raw pixel coordinates, and not "PASS/FAIL" against each language's own spec in isolation) — HE's "Client Type = position 1 from inline-start" must be directly compared against EN's "Client Type = position ? from inline-start"; any mismatch is a FAIL regardless of whether each side individually renders correctly relative to its own written instructions. This task's own verification script implements exactly this: it reads each element's physical `left` coordinate, sorts by `direction`-aware inline-start ordering (RTL: highest-`left`-first; LTR: lowest-`left`-first), and compares the resulting semantic sequence between HE and EN directly — not visual inspection alone.

**Status**: the corrected Mobile ordering is **IMPLEMENTED / TEST-VERIFIED / AWAITING OWNER VISUAL APPROVAL** — not automatically Owner-LOCKED by virtue of being implemented and tested. The permanent **rule** documented in this section (§63 itself) is Owner-established and takes effect immediately as a standing constraint on all future work, independent of whether this specific Mobile Quote History correction has yet received final Owner visual approval.

Whether project-level removal is supported/safe**: **UNKNOWN with a disclosed limitation** — this session's Vercel CLI is not authenticated (`vercel whoami` returns "Logged out"), so the actual Vercel project Domains configuration could not be read directly; no Vercel API/Dashboard evidence was available. Based on general Vercel platform architecture (not verified this session, explicitly flagged as such): every Vercel project is automatically provisioned a project-name-based `.vercel.app` domain that mirrors Production, and this default alias is not typically a per-project toggle that can be fully de-provisioned while the project remains actively deployed — but this was **not confirmed** and should not be treated as verified fact. **Recommended next step for this specific question**: Owner directly inspects Vercel Dashboard Project Settings Domains section, or grants this session authenticated Vercel access for a separately-scoped follow-up read.

**4. Whether legacy-link compatibility favors redirect first**: **YES, a real (not hypothetical) reason was found.** Two genuine application-code dependencies on the *current browsing origin* were confirmed via direct source read: (a) password reset (Supabase's password-recovery call, four call sites across `App.jsx`, `AppLocal.jsx`, `AppGlobal.jsx`, `Dashboard.jsx`) all use the browser's own current origin dynamically, not a hardcoded canonical value; (b) business-user-generated Public Quote "Copy Link"/WhatsApp-share links (`Dashboard.jsx`, `QuotesTab.jsx`) also use the browser's own current origin dynamically. A user who requests a password reset, or a business owner who shares a quote link, while browsing via `quotecode.vercel.app` gets a link embedding that exact origin. Immediately de-provisioning the domain would break any such link already in flight or already shared with a real customer; a proper HTTP redirect (path+query preserved, and browsers natively preserve URL fragments across a redirect when the target does not specify its own) would instead gracefully forward these to canonical. **This is the real reason favoring redirect-first, per the task's own explicit instruction not to choose removal merely for aesthetic cleanliness if existing links would break.** By contrast, signup confirmation and every transactional email link (quote delivery, trial/subscription expiration) are already hardcoded to canonical and carry zero risk either way — confirmed via direct source read, including an existing code comment already documenting exactly this rationale for the signup case.

**5. Recommended final domain architecture**: **C — STAGED REDIRECT, THEN LATER REMOVAL** (not immediate removal, not permanent redirect-only). See this task's Claude report for the full decision matrix and rationale. **Not implemented — recommendation only.**

**6. Auth/session impact of redirecting (not removing) `quotecode.vercel.app`**: a same-project redirect at the HTTP/edge layer (before the app or Supabase Auth ever sees the request) has no session-storage or cross-origin implication — Supabase sessions are stored in the browser's own storage, scoped per-origin; a user who has an existing session under one origin would need to sign in again under the other after being redirected (an origin change always requires this, by browser design — not new risk introduced by consolidation). The **multi-device requirement is fully preserved either way**: nothing about this consolidation touches Supabase's refresh-token/session model, which already treats every browser/device as an independent session regardless of which domain is used to reach the app.

## §66. Live Interactive ChatGPT Review Access — Architecture/Options Audit + Key Root-Cause Finding — NO IMPLEMENTATION (added 2026-08-31, Live Interactive ChatGPT Review Access task)

**Owner requirement**: ChatGPT must be able to review the Landing Pages live and interactively (scroll, follow navigation, inspect CTAs, replay for future changes) — a static screenshot/video package is fallback only, not the target end-state.

**KEY FINDING — likely true root cause of ChatGPT's fetch failure, directly reproduced, not merely theorized**: ProFlow's Landing Page is a 100% client-side-rendered React SPA with zero server-side rendering or prerendering anywhere in the stack — confirmed by reading the raw, unrendered HTML served by both `www.quotecodepro.com` and `quotecode.vercel.app`: the `<body>` contains only `<div id="root"></div>` and a minimal 2-3-line `<noscript>` fallback; every visible element of the actual Landing Page (hero, pricing, FAQ, features) is injected by `index-*.js` after it loads and executes in a real browser. The repository's only Edge Middleware (`middleware.ts`) does nothing but set a geolocation hint cookie on `/` — there is no prerendering-for-bots mechanism, no SSR, no SSG anywhere in this codebase. **This was independently reproduced this task** using this session's own AI-driven web-fetch tool (a different tool than ChatGPT's, but the same general category — content-retrieval-and-read, not full JS execution) against `www.quotecodepro.com/en`: it reported back "the page appears to be a loading shell or minimal content state," seeing only the page title, none of the actual marketing content — the same class of symptom the Owner described for ChatGPT. Separately, robots.txt (`Allow: /` for all user-agents, all paths), response headers, and User-Agent-varied `curl` requests were all checked and found completely clean — no WAF/bot-challenge, no UA-based blocking, no crawler restriction of any kind. This rules out deliberate blocking as the cause and strongly points to the missing-SSR/SSG architecture instead.

**Critical implication for every option below**: this root cause is **orthogonal to which Vercel host/domain/protection-setting serves the page** — `www.quotecodepro.com`, `quotecode.vercel.app`, a new preview deployment, and a hypothetical `review.quotecodepro.com` would all serve the **identical client-rendered bundle** and would therefore likely all fail the same way for a non-JS-executing fetch client, regardless of domain or authentication configuration. Solving the domain/protection dimension (what this task and the prior one were scoped to) does not by itself solve the rendering dimension. This is disclosed as the single most important finding of this task, going beyond the literal scope of the requested option matrix, because every option's real-world viability depends on it.

**Vercel-native mechanisms researched (current documentation, not assumed from memory)**: **Shareable Links** (a secure per-deployment link letting external viewers bypass Vercel Authentication without their own Vercel account — but the exact interaction pattern, e.g., a client-side redirect/cookie exchange, was not verified to be compatible with a non-browser fetch client). **Protection Bypass for Automation** (a secret bypass token passed as a header or `?x-vercel-protection-bypass=` query param — functional, but the token is itself a credential; pasting a URL containing it into a ChatGPT conversation would expose that credential outside ProFlow's control, in tension with "no secret required"). **Deployment Protection Exceptions** (marks a specific preview domain fully public, bypassing protection entirely for that domain — confirmed to require an Enterprise plan or the Advanced Deployment Protection add-on on Pro; **this project's actual plan tier was not verified this session**, since it requires Vercel Dashboard access this session does not have). **Preview Deployments are public by default** unless Deployment Protection is explicitly extended to the Preview environment — since the one deployment-specific URL tested (`quotecode-adp6tay5v-quote-code.vercel.app`, a Production-environment generated URL) was found SSO-protected, but the **current protection scope for the Preview environment specifically was not independently confirmed** (also requires Dashboard access).

**No implementation performed.** Full option matrix, recommended architecture, and staged (non-executed) implementation plan are recorded in this task's Claude report, not duplicated here in full — see there for the complete comparison.

**Recommendation summary**: (1) immediate, working today, zero further investigation needed — use the static review package already prepared in the prior task (screenshots + genuine demo-video files), since it fully sidesteps the rendering-dependency problem; (2) if genuine live interactivity is still required as a permanent capability, the real prerequisite is a **separate, dedicated future audit** of server-side-rendering/prerendering options for the Landing Page specifically (e.g., a build-time static-HTML snapshot, or bot-aware prerendering middleware) — not a Vercel domain/protection change — since no domain-only option is expected to solve the actual problem found here. This was not implemented and is recorded as a new candidate future item, not authorized work.

**Domain consolidation status unchanged**: `quotecode.vercel.app` remains exactly as it was; the staged-redirect recommendation (§64) remains pending and, per explicit instruction, sequenced to occur only after ChatGPT access is independently confirmed working — this task's own finding (that the rendering problem, not the domain, is likely the real blocker) is additional information for that sequencing decision, not a reason to change it.

## §67. Production Vercel Alias Redirect — IMPLEMENTED, LIVE, MOSTLY VERIFIED (one disclosed cache-propagation nuance) (added 2026-08-31, Production Vercel Alias Redirect task)

**`www.quotecodepro.com` is now, functionally as well as by intent, the sole ProFlow application origin. `quotecode.vercel.app` is a legacy-compatibility redirect only, not an independent second origin.**

**Implementation**: since this session has no authenticated Vercel Dashboard/API access (confirmed again fresh this task — `vercel whoami` → "Logged out"), the true Dashboard-configured domain-level redirect could not be used. Current Vercel documentation (looked up live this task, not assumed from memory) confirmed `vercel.json`'s `redirects` array supports a `has: [{type: "host", value: "..."}]` condition — a genuine Vercel edge-routing mechanism, evaluated before any application code runs, functionally equivalent to a Dashboard-configured domain redirect and explicitly distinct from an application-level React redirect. Added one rule: requests whose `Host` header is `quotecode.vercel.app` are redirected (`permanent: true` → HTTP 308) to the identical path and query on `https://www.quotecodepro.com`; requests to the canonical domain never match this rule (different host), so no redirect loop is possible by construction.

**Isolated commit**: `e03001745859ae6b81f162a4af5bdca3c95cac5a` on `main`, exactly one file (`vercel.json`, +10/-0), staged explicitly (never `-A`), pushed to `origin/main`. This does trigger a Vercel Production deploy (per the standing §17.E rule, disclosed) — confirmed completed via GitHub's own commit-status polling ("Deployment has completed") before any verification was attempted.

**Live verification — PASS for every tested path except the bare root**: `/he`, `/en`, `/public-quote/<id>`, `/en/public-quote/<id>?lang=en`, and `/dashboard` all correctly return `308` with the exact expected `Location`, and following the redirect lands on the correct final canonical URL with path **and** query string fully preserved (confirmed via `curl -L` showing `num_redirects:1` and the exact expected `url_effective`). The canonical domain (`www.quotecodepro.com` root/`/he`/`/en`) remains completely healthy and unaffected throughout.

**Disclosed anomaly, not hidden**: the bare root path (`https://quotecode.vercel.app/`) continued returning a stale, pre-redirect cached `200 OK` for several minutes after deployment completed (`X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `Age` growing monotonically past 270 seconds across repeated checks) — a CDN cache-propagation delay specific to that one already-cached URL, not a configuration defect. The redirect *rule* itself is proven correct and active by every other tested path (including the structurally-identical `/dashboard`), so this is assessed as a cache-serving nuance expected to self-resolve, not a failure of the implementation. No Vercel cache purge or additional deploy was attempted this task (no authenticated access to do so safely, and not clearly within this task's explicit authorization) — **the Owner should re-check the bare root path after some additional time, or trigger a cache purge/redeploy via the Vercel Dashboard if immediate resolution is desired.**

**No Supabase change was required or made.** Session/auth behavior is unaffected by this change beyond the expected, pre-existing origin-change requirement (a session tied to one origin doesn't transfer to another — inherent browser behavior, not new risk; see §64's prior analysis, unchanged). **No application code (`.jsx`/`.js`) was touched.** **No unrelated Vercel setting was changed** — the diff is exactly the one redirect rule, nothing else in `vercel.json` was modified.

**`quotecode.vercel.app` itself was NOT removed or de-provisioned** — per explicit instruction, this task implements the redirect only; removal remains optional and deferred, to be considered later only after legacy-link dependence has faded.

**Follow-up read-only re-check (same day, Vercel Root Redirect Final Read-Only Verification task)**: the bare root path was re-tested, fresh, with zero configuration/cache/deploy action taken (explicitly read-only). Still stale: identical `Etag` to the original pre-redirect response, `Age` at 653 seconds and climbing, `X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, no `Location` header, `0` redirects when followed. `/he` and `/en` continue to redirect correctly; canonical root remains healthy. Per explicit instruction, no cache purge/redeploy/config change was attempted. **VERCEL DOMAIN CONSOLIDATION STATUS: PARTIALLY VERIFIED, NOT YET CLOSED** — every path redirects correctly except the bare root, which requires either further natural cache expiry or an Owner-initiated Vercel Dashboard cache purge/redeploy (outside this session's available access) to resolve.

## §68. Landing-Page Prerender/SSR Feasibility Audit — AUDIT ONLY, NO IMPLEMENTATION (added 2026-08-31, Landing-Page Prerender/SSR Feasibility Audit task)

**Scope**: exactly `/`, `/he`, `/en` (Landing Pages, assets, videos, public marketing SEO surface) — Dashboard, Public Quote, Admin, signature flow, and every other authenticated/dynamic surface explicitly out of scope and untouched.

**Confirmed current state**: `main.jsx` mounts via React 18's `createRoot(...).render(...)` — a pure client-render call, not `hydrateRoot`. This means the app does not attempt hydration at all today; it fully replaces whatever is in `#root` on every load. This is favorable for the recommended option below: adding prerendered static markup inside `#root` carries **no React hydration-mismatch risk**, since the client never tries to reconcile against it — it simply re-renders over it exactly as it already does today for real browsers (a real browser sees, at most, an imperceptible instant swap from prerendered markup to freshly client-rendered markup — same visual result either way).

**Confirmed the Landing components are already SSR-safe as written, with zero code changes required for this property specifically**: every `window.`/`document.`/`navigator.` reference in `LandingLocal.jsx`/`LandingGlobal.jsx` is inside a `useEffect` (confirmed via direct source read) — React never runs effects during server-side rendering, so `react-dom/server`'s `renderToString` can already render these components today without throwing. The Landing Pages have **zero live/dynamic data dependency** (no Supabase calls, no `fetch`, only local UI-interaction state for the billing-cycle toggle/FAQ-accordion/accessibility-panel) — all marketing copy, pricing, and FAQ text is embedded directly in the component source, meaning a build-time static snapshot can never silently go stale relative to a rebuild.

**React Router v7's own native "Pre-Rendering" feature was investigated and ruled out for this codebase specifically** (not generically) — confirmed via current official documentation: it is explicitly "Framework Mode only," unavailable in "Declarative Mode" (`<BrowserRouter>`/`<Routes>`/`<Route>`). This project's actual routing (confirmed via direct source read of `AppGlobal.jsx`/`AppLocal.jsx`/`App.jsx`) uses exactly Declarative Mode. Adopting React Router's native prerendering would require migrating the entire app's routing architecture to Framework Mode — a full-app change, not a Landing-only one, and explicitly out of this task's scope ("do NOT propose or begin a full ProFlow SSR migration").

**Third-party SPA-prerendering plugins were checked and found unsuitable**: `prerender-spa-plugin` (the historically common choice) is archived/unmaintained since 2023. `vite-plugin-prerender` has unconfirmed current maintenance. `vite-react-ssg` is actively maintained but its own documentation recommends React Router v7 projects use React Router's own native capability instead (which is itself disqualified above) — introducing it would add a maintained-but-narrower-fit dependency for no real benefit over the option below.

**Recommended architecture — a small, self-contained, official-pattern build step, not a third-party plugin**: Vite's own official SSR guide documents exactly this pattern as a first-class, framework-endorsed technique — a minimal Node "entry-server" script that imports only `LandingLocal`/`LandingGlobal` (not the full app/router), wraps each in `StaticRouter` (react-router-dom's own purpose-built component for exactly this: server-rendering at a fixed URL with no real browser navigation), calls `react-dom/server`'s `renderToString`, and writes the result into the existing `dist/index.html`/per-path HTML output for `/`, `/he`, `/en` only. Built via Vite's own `vite build --ssr <entry>` mode, run as an additional build step alongside (not replacing) the existing `vite build`. No new runtime dependency, no change to the Dashboard/Public-Quote/Admin routes, no change to `main.jsx`'s existing client-render behavior for real browsers.

**Full option matrix, priority-ranked recommendation, and staged (unexecuted) implementation plan are recorded in this task's Claude report — not duplicated here in full.**

**Status**: audit only. No code was written or changed. No dependency was installed. No build was run. No deploy occurred. Owner + ChatGPT authorization required before any implementation phase begins.

## §76. Permanent Rule — Browser Harness Tab Hygiene (added 2026-08-31, Desktop HE/EN Mirroring task, Owner mid-task instruction)

**The rule, effective immediately and permanently**: during Browser Harness QA, open only the minimum number of tabs/pages required for the current verification; reuse an existing QA tab/page for locale, viewport, and route changes whenever practical rather than opening a new tab per case; close temporary tabs once a test case is complete; and — critically — **perform mandatory browser cleanup at the end of every task**: close every tab/page Claude/Browser Harness opened for that task (and any clearly-stale automation tabs left by prior runs), never touching the Owner's own personal browser tabs or unrelated sessions. A task that finishes its QA but leaves unnecessary Claude-created tabs open has **not** completed browser cleanup — cleanup is part of task completion, not optional follow-up.

**Why**: the Owner's machine was under heavy load (fan running hard) from RAM consumption by dozens of accumulated Claude-created QA tabs across this session's prior tasks — confirmed directly this task: a `list_tabs()` check mid-task found **34 open tabs**, nearly all stale `localhost:4173`/`localhost:5186`/temporary-Vercel-preview tabs left over from prior tasks' Landing-prerender and Dashboard QA. 32 were closed immediately at the Owner's urgent request, consolidating to exactly the 1-2 tabs genuinely needed for the remainder of this task's work.

**Important secondary finding from this same cleanup**: reusing an old tab across a locale switch surfaced a real testing-methodology risk worth recording — `localhost:5186`'s two dashboard tabs share the same browser origin, so logging into a different TEST account on one tab silently changes the Supabase session for **every** tab on that origin (no per-tab isolation). Reusing a stale tab after switching accounts on another tab produces mixed/stale state (e.g., one tab briefly showed the INTL account's email with HE UI text and cached LOCAL-account row data simultaneously). The safe pattern going forward: when a task's QA requires switching between different TEST accounts, always do a full `localStorage.clear()` + fresh navigation + fresh login before measuring on ANY tab, never assume a previously-authenticated tab's session is still valid for its original account after any other same-origin tab has since logged in as someone else.

**Status**: permanent operational rule, in effect for all future Browser Harness sessions on this project.

- **RED**: two distinct underlying causes render identically — (a) `quote.email_bounced` is true (the recipient address doesn't exist / the message bounced, detected asynchronously by a `resend-email-webhook`, not by the immediate send result — stays red until a successful resend, per the function's own comment), or (b) `emailStatus` is truthy but not `'success'` (the immediate send attempt itself failed). Tooltip differs per cause ("כתובת המייל ששלחת אינה קיימת"/"The email address you sent does not exist" for bounced; "שליחת האימייל נכשלה"/"Email failed" for a failed send).
- **GREEN**: `emailStatus === 'success'` — the email was sent successfully.
- **BLANK** (no dot rendered at all): both `quote.email_bounced` is falsy and `emailStatus` is null/undefined — no email has been sent for this quote yet (no entry exists in the `emailStatuses` map for it).

Since the table uses the browser default `table-layout: auto` (not `fixed`), `width` is a sizing hint the browser will still expand past if content genuinely demands it — this is a safety property, not a defect: no data can ever be clipped or hidden by this width value, worst case is a less-than-ideal column width on an unusually long value, which does not occur with this data's actual format.

## §74. Hot Quote Fixed Geometry / No Layout Shift — IMPLEMENTED, TEST-VERIFIED, LOCAL/UNCOMMITTED (added 2026-08-31, Hot Quote Fixed Geometry task)

**Owner requirement**: the Hot Quote ("הצעה חמה") card's 4-second rotation among qualifying quotes must never change Dashboard geometry — long content should truncate, not push the page.

**Root cause, confirmed by source read before any code change**: `Dashboard.jsx`'s Hot Quote card (`.dash-kpi-card.dash-kpi-hot`, inside the `.dash-kpi-grid` CSS Grid, `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px,1fr))`) rotates every 4 seconds among quotes with `view_count >= 3` and not approved/paid (`setHotQuoteIndex`, an existing `setInterval` effect keyed on `[quotes]`). The message text (`t.hotQuoteAlert(currentHotClientName, currentHotViewCount)`) embeds the rotating quote's real client `company_name` — a free-text field of unbounded length. The card's text column had no `minHeight` and the message `div` (`.dash-kpi-sub`) had no line-clamp/overflow control — so every rotation, a longer or shorter company name changed the number of wrapped lines, which changed the card's height, which (CSS Grid's default `align-items: stretch` plus ordinary block flow below the grid) visibly shifted every Dashboard section beneath the KPI row. No CSS file references any `dash-kpi-*` class (confirmed via repo-wide grep) — all styling is inline in the JSX, so the fix is fully self-contained to this one block.

**Files changed**: `src/pages/Dashboard.jsx` (the Hot Quote card JSX block only, `dash-kpi-hot` search-anchor, ~10 net lines) — no other part of this file (which already carried substantial unrelated pre-existing uncommitted changes from earlier sessions, confirmed via `git diff --stat` before and after: pre-existing 347/-76 → 357/-79, exactly matching this task's own addition) was touched. New file: `src/pages/Dashboard.hotquote.test.js` (regression guard, see below).

**Implementation** (narrowest correction, no redesign): the text-column `<div>` wrapping the card's label + message now carries `minHeight: '52px'` and `justifyContent: 'center'` (so short content sits centered within the reserved space rather than pinned to the top with visible dead space below); the message `<div>` (`.dash-kpi-sub`) now carries the standard CSS line-clamp pattern (`display: '-webkit-box', WebkitLineClamp: 2, WebkitBoxOrient: 'vertical', overflow: 'hidden'`), capping it at exactly 2 lines regardless of content length. Together these make the card's total height constant: content shorter than the reserved space no longer collapses it, content longer than 2 lines is truncated (native browser ellipsis) rather than growing it. No typography, color, spacing, icon, copy, animation, surrounding-card, or business-logic change was made — the rotation mechanism itself, the message template, and the qualifying-quote filter are all untouched.

**Geometry-stability evidence — real browser, real DOM measurement, not inferred**: rather than waiting on live rotation timing, verified directly by injecting extreme long-text and short-text content into the actual rendered `.dash-kpi-sub` node (via `element.textContent =`, a one-time DOM write for measurement purposes only — the real React-owned content and rotation mechanism were never modified) and comparing `getBoundingClientRect()` of the card, the grid, and a fixed reference element (the search input) below it, before and after, on **real TEST data** logged into both the LOCAL (HE) and INTL (EN) TEST accounts (`PROFLOW_TEST_LOCAL_*` / `PROFLOW_TEST_INTL_*`, the established precedented TEST-only credential pair already stored in the gitignored `.env`/`.env.localtest.local` files — read directly from disk within the verification script, never printed to any log, screenshot, report, or continuity file, per explicit Owner instruction). Result, identical pattern across all 8 combinations below: card/grid `top` and `height` were **byte-for-byte identical** across baseline real content, extreme injected long text (confirmed the line-clamp actually engages — `scrollHeight` ~83-100px of unclamped content vs `clientHeight` capped at exactly 33px, i.e., ~3 lines of real content actively suppressed), and extreme injected short text. Screenshots taken at every step visually confirm clean 2-line ellipsis truncation (with the ellipsis correctly appearing at the RTL-correct edge for HE) and no card-boundary change.

**Responsive QA matrix — all 8 combinations PASS** (viewports: Desktop 1920×1080 native window; Mobile 390×844 @3x; Tablet Portrait 768×1024 @2x; Tablet Landscape 1024×768 @2x — all via CDP `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` against the real running TEST dev server, `npm run dev:localtest` on port 5186, an already-running pre-existing instance from an earlier session, reused as-is): HE Desktop, EN Desktop, HE Mobile, EN Mobile, HE Tablet Portrait, EN Tablet Portrait, HE Tablet Landscape, EN Tablet Landscape — zero geometry change under long/short text injection on every combination, zero horizontal overflow (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` confirmed true) on every combination. RTL (HE) and LTR (EN) both confirmed correct throughout, including the correct mirrored placement of unrelated card/nav elements already established in prior tasks (not touched, not regressed).

**Long-text behavior**: confirmed truncation is the actual outcome for both HE and EN extreme-length synthetic company names (150-190 characters) — no existing tooltip/title/full-text-on-hover UX exists for this element, and none was invented, per explicit instruction ("Do NOT invent new UX unless necessary" / "A few hidden characters are acceptable").

**Regression protection added**: `src/pages/Dashboard.hotquote.test.js` — two new Vitest tests, not a full-Dashboard-mount test (mounting the real `Dashboard.jsx` default export would require disproportionate Supabase/auth/routing mocking for a monolithic, non-decomposed authenticated-page component with no existing unit-test harness — confirmed by reading `QuotesTab.test.jsx`'s established pattern, which only works because `QuotesTab` is already a props-driven, decomposed component, unlike `Dashboard.jsx`). Instead, a narrow source-level regression guard: reads `Dashboard.jsx`'s own source text, extracts the Hot Quote JSX block, and asserts the `minHeight: '52px'` and `WebkitLineClamp: 2` / `overflow: 'hidden'` properties remain present — this fails immediately if a future edit silently removes the geometry-stabilizing CSS, without needing to mount or mock the surrounding monolithic component. 72/72 total tests pass (70 pre-existing + 2 new). Lint: 0 errors (same 1 pre-existing unrelated `Dashboard.jsx` `loadData` dependency warning, already documented in prior tasks). Normal build: PASS.

**No regression observed** to Quote History, navigation, HE/EN directionality, or any other Dashboard section — all visually confirmed unaffected across all 8 screenshot captures taken this task.

**Part C — MARKET SEPARATION FAIL-CLOSED IRON RULE (PERMANENT, CANONICAL)**:

> **Local (Hebrew/RTL) and International (English/LTR) are semantically separate markets, not one market in two languages.**
>
> - **Local** = Hebrew, RTL, ILS/₪, Israeli VAT (מע"מ) and other Israeli-business-specific semantics.
> - **International** = English, LTR, USD/EUR/GBP only — **never** ₪, **never** an automatic inheritance of Israeli VAT/tax/business semantics.
> - **HE/EN parity means mirroring equivalent UX** (same layout, same interaction patterns, same information density) — it does **not** mean translating a Local-specific business concept into English. Concretely: `לפני מע"מ` (before-VAT) is an Israeli-tax-law concept; it must **not** automatically become an English `"Before VAT"` label or any other International-market feature unless that feature is independently specified and authorized for International on its own merits. (This is precisely why Part B's fix removed the dead `"Before VAT"` English branch entirely rather than "completing" it into a real feature — reviving it would have been exactly the mistake this rule forbids.)
>
> **Mandatory contradiction handling — applies to every agent (Owner instructions relayed secondhand, ChatGPT, Claude Lead, Agent HE, Agent EN, or any future coding agent)**: if any instruction, from any source, appears to require introducing a Local-specific business/tax/currency semantic into International (or vice versa) — including an instruction that merely *looks* like a translation/parity request but would actually carry business semantics across the market boundary — **do not implement that sub-item**. Fail closed: stop, report **"MARKET-SEPARATION CONFLICT"**, state exactly which instruction and which semantic appears to cross the boundary, and request explicit clarification before proceeding. This applies even if the conflicting instruction came from ChatGPT or from the Owner by accident — the rule exists specifically to catch cases where market-crossing was not the Owner's actual intent.

This rule is now canonical. Cross-referenced in `PROFLOW_TODO.md` item 34. No conflicting instruction was encountered this task — Parts A/B/D/E all remained within the existing market boundaries (Part A is HE+EN symmetric with no semantic content; Part B is explicitly HE-only by the pre-existing, unchanged guard condition).

### Part B — Views Numeric Geometry: IMPLEMENTED, LIVE-VERIFIED

**Root cause** (Owner-reported): the Desktop/Mobile Views cell wrapped `[number, icon]` in an `inline-flex` with `justifyContent:'center'`, centering the *group* — since the group's own width grows with digit count, the icon's actual X position shifted row-to-row even though the column's own width never changed.

**Fix**: the number is now rendered in its own fixed-width sub-box (Desktop `22px`, Mobile `17px`), `textAlign:'right'` (deliberately **not** `isHebrew`-conditional — digit glyph order is always LTR even inside Hebrew text, so right-aligning the ones-place is the correct anchor in both directions, not a market-separation violation), with `fontVariantNumeric:'tabular-nums'` so every digit glyph occupies identical width (units/tens/hundreds place-value alignment). The icon carries `flexShrink:0`. Because the number sub-box is now fixed-width, the `[number-box + icon]` group's total width is constant regardless of value, so the surrounding `textAlign:'center'` on the `<td>` now centers a genuinely constant-width unit. DOM order (`[number, icon]`) was **not** changed — the existing `dir={tableDir}` on the table continues to mirror it automatically (number-then-icon from each locale's own inline-start, exactly the pre-existing established pattern). Desktop header width was widened `28px→46px` to match the new reserved body geometry (table-layout is `auto`, so the body content would have forced this width regardless — the header `width` is now an accurate hint, not a cap).

**Real-browser geometry proof** (`getBoundingClientRect()`, both locales, all 9 required boundary values `0,1,9,10,19,99,100,637,999` — 3-digit values obtained via safe temporary DOM-node text simulation where real TEST data topped out at 19, then reverted, confirmed `restored:true` each time):

| | Icon X | Number-box X | Constant across all 9 values? |
|---|---|---|---|
| HE Desktop (30 real rows, values 0-19) | 1350.81 | 1367.81 | Yes — identical across all 30 real rows |
| HE Desktop (simulated 3-digit, first row) | 1350.81 | 1367.81 | Yes — identical across all 9 boundary values, incl. 999 |
| EN Desktop (simulated, empty-account tbody) | 508.91 | 483.91 (EN: number precedes icon, mirrored) | Yes — identical across all 9 boundary values |
| HE Mobile card (6 real rows, values 0/1/2/19) | 322 | 303 | Yes — identical across all sampled rows |

Adjacent protected columns (Client Type, Order Number) and overall table width (`950px`) were also measured before/after simulating a `999` value in the Views cell — **byte-identical**, confirming zero layout disturbance to neighboring columns. No horizontal overflow observed at any point (Desktop, and both Mobile/Tablet-Portrait card layouts, both locales).

**Testing methodology note (self-correction during this task)**: an initial responsive-overflow pass using CDP `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` alone produced false-negative "no overflow" results at Mobile/Tablet-Portrait widths, because ProFlow's own `isMobileView` resize listener (documented in `QuotesTab.jsx` itself) does not always fire from CDP's viewport override alone — the desktop table (inside its own `overflow-x:auto` wrapper) was still silently rendering and simply not overflowing the *outer* page, which is not the same as confirming the mobile card layout. Corrected by explicitly dispatching `window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize'))` after each CDP override and confirming via `!!document.querySelector('table')` which layout was actually active before trusting the overflow reading. Documented here as a permanent testing-methodology note for future real-browser QA of this component.

### Part C — Order Number Sorting: FIXED, ROOT-CAUSED, LIVE-VERIFIED

**Root cause**: `Dashboard.jsx`'s quote sort comparator (`quoteSortField === 'id'` branch) compared `a.id`/`b.id` — the row's internal Supabase UUID primary key — which has **no relationship whatsoever** to the displayed Order Number (`formatQuoteFallback(quote)` → `A${quote.quote_number}`, e.g. `A100713`). In practice this sorted by effectively-random UUID string, not by the sequence the user actually sees.

**Fix**: extracted a new pure, exported, independently-unit-tested function `getQuoteOrderSortKey(quote)` in `src/utils/quoteNumber.js` (co-located with `formatQuoteFallback`, the single source of truth for how the order number is derived/displayed) that returns a numeric sort key from `quote.quote_number` directly. Legacy quotes without a real `quote_number` yet (displayed via the pre-existing `#UUID-prefix` fallback) have no meaningful numeric order position — they are placed as one group entirely before every real-numbered quote (`LEGACY_ORDER_CEILING = 1e15`, far above both any realistic `quote_number` and any `created_at` epoch-ms value), and sorted among themselves by `created_at` so their own relative order is still meaningful rather than arbitrary. `Dashboard.jsx`'s `id` branch now simply calls this function for `aVal`/`bVal` — the surrounding generic ascending/descending comparator logic was **not** rewritten, per explicit instruction to fix the narrowest root cause.

**Regression tests** (`src/utils/quoteNumber.test.js`, new file, 6 tests): ascending by real `quote_number`; descending (exact reverse); no lexicographic-string trap across digit-count boundaries (`A10 < A9` as strings but `10 > 9` numerically — explicitly tested with `9,10,99,100,999,1000`); never uses `id`/UUID as a sort signal; legacy-quotes-group-before-real-numbered-quotes; legacy quotes ordered among themselves by `created_at`.

**Live-verified** on real TEST data (30 real quotes, `A100700`-`A100732`, some gaps): clicking the Order header produced `A100700, A100701, A100703, A100704, ...` ascending (correct numeric sequence, confirmed **not** the pre-fix UUID-random order); clicking again produced `A100732, A100731, A100730, A100729, ...` descending (exact reverse). Displayed Order Number format and order-number generation logic were **not** changed — only the sort comparator's data source.
